Name: Comments
Summary: Comments below posts, events or pages, and guestbooks. New messages wait for approval unless moderation is off, and staff can reply from the admin.
Guide:
Every message belongs to a subject: a text the template chooses, such as a post ID, a page ID or a fixed word. Add an instance per kind of conversation; each has its own messages, settings and admin section.

Add it to the site

app.Use(
    comments.Module("guestbook", "Guestbook"),
    comments.Module("remarks", "Comments"),
)

The key (guestbook) is the instance's name in URLs and template functions and must be unique on the site. The title (Guestbook) is what editors see in the admin navigation and the page editor.

Comments below content

Comments attach to anything with an ID through the template functions; the instance needs no page of its own. Below a post in news/post.gohtml:

{{commentThread "remarks" .ID}}

commentThread renders the approved comments on that subject, oldest first with their replies, followed by the form. {{commentForm "remarks" .ID}} renders only the form, and {{commentCount "remarks" .ID}} counts the approved comments and replies, for example next to titles in a list.

Both come with plain, accessible default markup. A theme replaces them with remarks/thread.gohtml and remarks/form.gohtml, or comments/thread.gohtml and comments/form.gohtml for every instance; task templates -- remarks writes the defaults to start from. They use stable wt-* classes (wt-comments, wt-comment, wt-comment--staff, …), laid out by the optional stylesheet webthings.css, which the layout links with {{styles "webthings.css" "site.css"}} (see The base stylesheet). Their texts go through tl, so the site's translations translate them.

For markup of your own, comments returns the approved comments, commentURL the address the form posts to, commentInput the form's model for a subject, commentResult the outcome of the visitor's last post and commentsClosed whether new comments are refused:

{{range comments "remarks" .ID}}
    <article>
        <strong>{{.Name}}</strong> {{date .CreatedAt}}
        {{.HTML}}

        {{range .Replies}}
            <blockquote>{{if .Staff}}Reply from the site:{{else}}{{.Name}}:{{end}} {{.HTML}}</blockquote>
        {{end}}
    </article>
{{end}}

<div id="remarks">
    {{with commentResult "remarks"}}<p class="notice">{{.}}</p>{{end}}

    {{if not (commentsClosed "remarks")}}
        {{with commentInput "remarks" .ID}}
            {{form_open .}}
                {{form_field . "subject" nil}}
                {{form_field . "name" nil}}
                {{form_field . "email" nil}}
                {{form_field . "body" nil}}
                <button>Send</button>
            {{form_close}}
        {{end}}
    {{end}}
</div>

HTML is the message escaped, with its paragraphs and line breaks. CreatedAt is in UTC; {{date .CreatedAt}} shows it in the page's language and the site's timezone.

form_open writes the form tag, posting to commentURL, with the spam trap and the page to return to: the element whose id is the instance key, here remarks. form_field renders one field of the form by its key, with its label, its limits (required, maxlength) and its help text, translated with the site's translations and in the site's form theme; subject is a hidden field with the subject. The fields' ids start with the key, such as remarks-name. See Template functions. Inputs written by hand with the same names work too.

Guestbook page

In the admin, open a page and choose the instance under Shows on this page. The page renders guestbook/list.gohtml, or comments/list.gohtml for every instance without a design of its own, with a comments.ListView: the approved messages of the instance, newest first, 20 per page. .Form is the form, with .Subject, the instance key, as its subject: {{form_open .Form}} with form_field per field, subject included, returns the visitor to the element whose id is .Key. The pager's .NewerURL and .OlderURL are the page's address with ?page=, such as /en/guestbook?page=2. Generate a starting point with:

task templates -- guestbook

The form component works here too:

{{/* @dot github.com/donseba/go-webthings/modules/comments.ListView */}}
<h1>{{.Title}}</h1>

{{commentForm .Key .Subject}}

{{range .Comments}}
    <article>
        <p><strong>{{.Name}}</strong> · {{date .CreatedAt}}</p>
        {{.HTML}}
    </article>
{{end}}

{{with .NewerURL}}<a href="{{.}}">Newer</a>{{end}}
{{with .OlderURL}}<a href="{{.}}">Older</a>{{end}}

The page lists the messages of every subject of the instance, so keep a guestbook apart from the comments below posts.

Visitors

The form posts to /_/<key>/post ({{commentURL "remarks"}}) with the fields of comments.PostInput:

Field
subject required, one line, at most 200 characters
name required, one line, at most 100 characters
email optional; never shown on the website
body required, plain text, at most 5,000 characters
parent optional: the ID of the comment to answer; a reply to a reply joins the same thread

form_open adds the spam trap and the page to return to, the element whose id is the instance key. The visitor comes back with ?<key>=<result>, which commentResult and the form component read:

  • sent: the message is shown right away;
  • pending: it waits for approval;
  • invalid: a field is missing, too long or not on one line;
  • closed: the instance was closed for new messages when the visitor posted; the form component says so even after it opens again;
  • throttled: the visitor posted more than 5 times in 10 minutes.

With invalid, the form shows what the visitor wrote again, with a message in the page's language at each field to correct. The components and form_field do this without a change to the template; inputs written by hand do not. Of several comment forms on one page, only the one for the subject the visitor wrote on shows it. See A post with mistakes. A post that cannot be saved, such as when the database cannot be reached, gets the site's error page, 500.gohtml, also with HTMX.

Bots that fill in the spam trap get the answer a person would get; nothing is stored. A post that stores nothing, spam, invalid, closed or throttled, leaves the pages in the site's output cache as they are; see Modules and the output cache. The message's language is the language of the page it was written on. Visitors' IP addresses are never stored: a hash that changes daily lets moderators spot a flood from one sender.

Moderation

The instance's admin section (/admin/remarks; /admin is the default admin path) lists the messages newest first, grouped by subject, with tabs for pending, approved and all messages. A group is headed by the title of the published content on the page its messages were written on, such as a post's title, with the page's address below it; when messages were written in several languages, the page in the admin's language wins. Without published content there the heading is the address, and a guestbook's is the instance's title. Each message shows the name, the e-mail address, the language, the page it was written on and a short sender code. The badge in the navigation counts the messages that are not shown.

  • Approve shows a message, Hide takes it off the website again, after the question "Take this off the website?". Both need the publish right.
  • Reply adds a staff reply, shown at once and marked as Staff. It is signed with the site title in the comment's language (or the organisation, or the editor's name) and approves the comment it answers. It needs the create right.
  • Move to trash moves a message and its replies to the trash, where they can be restored or deleted for good; restoring the message brings its replies back with it. It needs the delete right. A reply deleted on its own cannot be restored while the message it answers is in the trash.

Under Settings, editors with the edit right switch Approve messages before they are shown (on by default), close the instance with Closed for new messages, and set a Notification address.

E-mail

With a notification address, every new message from a visitor is mailed there in the admin's language: the name and address, the message, the page it was written on, whether it waits for approval, and a link to the admin. Replying to the mail answers the visitor when they gave an address.

The mail is the template notify, with a comments.NotifyView. A theme replaces it with mail/remarks/notify.gohtml, or mail/comments/notify.gohtml for every instance; task templates -- remarks writes the default there.

From Go

comments.Of(app, "remarks") returns the instance once the app has started:

remarks := comments.Of(app, "remarks")

list, err := remarks.List(ctx, postID)
count, err := remarks.Count(ctx, postID)

Add stores a message after the same checks as the form, for example in an import; Reply, Approve and Delete do what the admin does, and Undelete and Purge bring a deleted message back or remove it for good. What they change shows on the site at once, also on pages in the site's output cache; see Modules and the output cache. CreatedAt keeps the original date; zero means now. A reply passes the ID of the comment Add returned as ParentID:

comment, err := remarks.Add(ctx, comments.Entry{
    Subject:   postID,
    Name:      "Anna",
    Body:      "Great to see the playground open again.",
    Locale:    "en",
    Approved:  true,
    CreatedAt: written,
})

reply, err := remarks.Add(ctx, comments.Entry{
    Subject:  postID,
    ParentID: comment.ID,
    Name:     "Ben",
    Body:     "The swings are new too.",
    Locale:   "en",
    Approved: true,
})

Related modules

  • Publishing and Events give comments a subject: a post's or event's ID.
  • Registrations attaches sign-ups to events in the same way.
  • Forms receives messages for the site's staff only, with an inbox.

SQL.Name: postgres
SQL.SQL:
-- Visitor comments and guestbook entries. subject is what a comment belongs
-- to, chosen by the template: a post ID, a page path or a fixed word. A reply
-- points at its top-level comment; staff replies are written in the admin.
-- ip_hash is a keyed, daily-changing hash of the address, only for spotting
-- floods; the address itself is never stored.
-- Deleting moves a message to the trash (deleted_at); its replies go along
-- with the same deleted_at and come back with it.
CREATE TABLE wt_comment (
    id         UUID PRIMARY KEY,
    instance   VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    subject    VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    parent_id  UUID REFERENCES wt_comment (id) ON DELETE CASCADE,
    name       VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    email      VARCHAR(254) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    body       TEXT NOT NULL,
    locale     VARCHAR(35) NOT NULL,
    page_path  VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    approved   BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    is_staff   BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    ip_hash    VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    created_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    created_by UUID,
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    updated_by UUID,
    deleted_at TIMESTAMPTZ,
    deleted_by UUID
);

CREATE INDEX wt_comment_subject ON wt_comment (instance, subject, created_at);

CREATE INDEX wt_comment_review ON wt_comment (instance, approved, created_at);

CREATE INDEX wt_comment_parent ON wt_comment (parent_id);

-- Settings per instance; an instance without a row uses the defaults
-- (moderated, open, no notification).
CREATE TABLE wt_comment_setting (
    instance   VARCHAR(64) PRIMARY KEY,
    moderated  BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    closed     BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    notify     VARCHAR(254) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    updated_at TIMESTAMPTZ NOT NULL,
    updated_by UUID
);

SQL.Name: mysql
SQL.SQL:
-- Visitor comments and guestbook entries. subject is what a comment belongs
-- to, chosen by the template: a post ID, a page path or a fixed word. A reply
-- points at its top-level comment; staff replies are written in the admin.
-- ip_hash is a keyed, daily-changing hash of the address, only for spotting
-- floods; the address itself is never stored.
-- Deleting moves a message to the trash (deleted_at); its replies go along
-- with the same deleted_at and come back with it.
CREATE TABLE wt_comment (
    id         VARCHAR(36) PRIMARY KEY,
    instance   VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL,
    subject    VARCHAR(200) NOT NULL,
    parent_id  VARCHAR(36) NULL,
    name       VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
    email      VARCHAR(254) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    body       TEXT NOT NULL,
    locale     VARCHAR(35) NOT NULL,
    page_path  VARCHAR(500) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    approved   BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    is_staff   BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    ip_hash    VARCHAR(64) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    created_at DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    created_by VARCHAR(36) NULL,
    updated_at DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    updated_by VARCHAR(36) NULL,
    deleted_at DATETIME(6) NULL,
    deleted_by VARCHAR(36) NULL,
    INDEX wt_comment_subject (instance, subject, created_at),
    INDEX wt_comment_review (instance, approved, created_at),
    FOREIGN KEY (parent_id) REFERENCES wt_comment (id) ON DELETE CASCADE
) ENGINE=InnoDB;

-- Settings per instance; an instance without a row uses the defaults
-- (moderated, open, no notification).
CREATE TABLE wt_comment_setting (
    instance   VARCHAR(64) PRIMARY KEY,
    moderated  BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT TRUE,
    closed     BOOLEAN NOT NULL DEFAULT FALSE,
    notify     VARCHAR(254) NOT NULL DEFAULT '',
    updated_at DATETIME(6) NOT NULL,
    updated_by VARCHAR(36) NULL
) ENGINE=InnoDB;

Types.Doc: InboxRow is one message in the admin list.
Types.Decl:
type InboxRow struct {
	Date   string
	Name   string
	Email  string
	Locale string
	Body   string
	// PageURL is the page the message was written on.
	PageURL  string
	ReplyTo  string
	Staff    bool
	Approved bool
	// Sender is a short code that is equal for messages from one address on
	// one day.
	Sender   string
	Approve  *form.RenderModel
	Hide     *form.RenderModel
	Delete   *form.RenderModel
	ReplyURL string
}

Types.Name: PostInput
Types.Doc: PostInput is the form a visitor posts to /_/<key>/post: the subject the message belongs to, optionally the message it answers, a name, an optional e-mail address and the message. Themes render its fields with form_field, with their limits ({{form_field .Form "name" nil}}, see ListView, FormView and commentInput), or write inputs with these names.
Types.Decl:
type PostInput struct {
	Subject string `form:"input,hidden" name:"subject" required:"true" maxLength:"200"  line:"true"`
	Parent  string `form:"input,hidden" name:"parent"                  maxLength:"64"   line:"true"`
	Name    string `form:"input,text"   name:"name"    required:"true" maxLength:"100"  line:"true" label:"Name"           autocomplete:"name"`
	Email   string `form:"input,email"  name:"email"                   maxLength:"254"              label:"E-mail address" autocomplete:"email" validate:"mail" description:"Optional, never shown on the website."`
	Body    string `form:"textarea"     name:"body"    required:"true" maxLength:"5000"             label:"Message"`
}
